name: Pages load only what they need

steps.title: BUDGET GATE (paired with step 2): 2500ms caps how long this navigation may silently absorb slow API calls -- demo_runner's goto waits for networkidle up to min(timeout_ms, 12000), so without this cap a multi-second /api/health regression would be swallowed here and step 2 would still pass instantly. Measured on this host: document ready 0.02-0.03s, full settle 1.24-1.29s

TC-5/TC-6/TC-12 -- GET /api/health answers with a real backend answer WITHIN BUDGET: the readiness badge's OWN data-state attribute reads ready (only true once GET /api/health has actually resolved with readiness="ready"), not a heading/title match, and it must be on screen no later than 2500ms (step 1's cap) + 2000ms = 4.5s after navigation start. Measured on this host: 1.24-1.29s end-to-end, /api/health itself 11-38ms in-browser

BUDGET GATE (paired with step 5): 2500ms caps this navigation's networkidle absorption so a slow bars read cannot be swallowed here. Measured on this host: document ready 0.03s, full settle 0.99-1.05s

TC-8/TC-9/TC-12 -- GET /api/stocks/AAPL/bars?through=latest answers with a real value WITHIN BUDGET: the chart-window caption (bar count + as-of date, rendered ONLY once the bars payload has resolved), not a heading/title match, and it must be on screen no later than 2500ms (step 4's cap) + 2000ms = 4.5s after navigation start -- 1.7s under the 6.2s Addendum 18 regression this gate exists to catch. Measured on this host: 0.99-1.05s end-to-end, the bars call itself 312-370ms in-browser

BUDGET GATE (paired with steps 9-10): 2500ms caps this navigation's networkidle absorption. Measured on this host: document ready 0.03-0.04s, full settle 0.93-1.01s (the availability call fires AFTER this, behind the page's own 2500ms stagger -- see step 9)

Deliberately consumes the frontend's OWN AVAILABILITY_FETCH_STAGGER_MS=2500 delay (apps/frontend/app/data/page.tsx) BEFORE starting step 10's budget clock -- without this wait, step 10's window would measure the stagger, not the call, and would falsely fail every replay regardless of backend speed

TC-1/TC-2/TC-3/TC-12 -- GET /api/data/availability answers with a real served payload WITHIN BUDGET: an availability-cell rendered from the response's cells[] (a warm/idle backend serves stale:false with non-empty cells), not a heading/title match, and it must be on screen no later than 2000ms after the page's own stagger has elapsed -- the tightest of the four gates, because step 9 has already consumed the product's own delay, so this window is effectively the availability call itself (32-38ms measured in-browser; 15.1-21.2s pre-fix, Addendum 18)

BUDGET GATE (paired with step 13): 2500ms caps this navigation's networkidle absorption so a slow /api/runs read cannot be swallowed here. Measured on this host: document ready 0.05-0.06s, full settle 1.45-1.46s

TC-11/TC-12 -- GET /api/runs answers with a real stored row WITHIN BUDGET: a run-history table row (only rendered once the grouped-aggregate n_stocks response resolves), not a heading/title match, and it must be on screen no later than 2500ms (step 12's cap) + 2000ms = 4.5s after navigation start -- 2.3s under the 6.8-10.7s pre-fix reading. Measured on this host: 1.51-1.54s end-to-end, the /api/runs call itself 203-464ms in-browser

ops-hardening iter-57 (TC-12, this iteration's own golden-teeth item): closes the iter-52 lesson's defect class for J-06 itself -- every step above only ever matched a static page heading, which the shell renders whether or not the underlying API call ever succeeded or was fast, so a real regression (e.g. Addendum 18's 6.2s bars read, or 241ms health) would have silently PASSED this golden forever. FOUR new dedicated steps (2, 5, 10, 13) were added, one per historically over-budget endpoint (GET /api/health, GET /api/stocks/AAPL/bars?through=latest, GET /api/data/availability, GET /api/runs), each asserting a REAL value that only exists once its endpoint has actually answered (the readiness badge's own data-state="ready" attribute; the bars chart's own window-caption text; an availability-cell rendered from the response's cells[]; a run-history table row) -- never a bare heading.

ops-hardening iter-57 FIX PASS (reviewer CRITICAL, reports/reviews/goal-ops-hardening-iter-57-review.md): the four dedicated steps now carry REAL per-step budgets, and so do the four navigations that precede them. The first pass shipped them with NO per-step `timeout_ms`, inheriting this file's 8000ms default; the reviewer failed that as vacuous, and a controlled experiment CONFIRMED the reviewer was right: replaying the SAME golden with its `timeout_ms` values stripped, against a backend artificially slowed by +6200ms on `/api/stocks/{ticker}/bars` (the exact Addendum 18 regression this item exists to catch), PASSED. With the budgets below it FAILS, at step 05, naming that step. 
WHY A GATE NEEDS TWO STEPS, NOT ONE (the mechanism the first pass got wrong): demo_runner's `goto` waits for `networkidle` with `min(step timeout_ms, 12000)` and swallows the outcome (a networkidle timeout is best-effort, never a failure). So the navigation step ABSORBS a slow API call, and by the time the assertion step runs the value is already on screen -- measured here at 0.01-0.07s for all four assertion steps, whatever the endpoint actually cost. Tightening only the assertion step therefore cannot gate latency; the navigation's absorption window must be capped too. Each budgeted endpoint now gets a PAIR: the `goto` capped at 2500ms (bounding how much latency it may silently absorb) and the value assertion capped at 2000ms -- a 4.5s end-to-end tripwire from navigation start, 1.7s under the 6.2s bars regression and 2.3s under the 6.8-10.7s /api/runs reading. For /api/data/availability the gate is tighter still: step 9 has already consumed the product's own 2500ms stagger, so step 10's 2000ms window is effectively the availability call itself. 
SIZED FROM MEASUREMENT, NOT FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES (live, warm backend on 8257 + prod frontend on 3257, 3 runs, reports/perf-budgets.md Addendum 22): document-ready (the only HARD part of a `goto`) 0.02-0.06s -- so the 2500ms navigation cap carries a ~40x margin on what can actually fail it; full page settle (networkidle, i.e. every one of that page's API calls resolved) 0.93-1.46s; the assertion steps themselves 0.01-0.14s of their 2000ms windows. In-browser per-call timings on the same runs: /api/health 11-38ms, bars 312-370ms, /api/data/availability 32-38ms, /api/runs 203-464ms. 
PROVEN TO HAVE TEETH, ONE ENDPOINT AT A TIME (sabotage matrix, Addendum 22): a delaying reverse proxy in front of the real backend slowed ONE endpoint per run. +5000ms on /api/health -> FAIL at step 02; +6200ms on bars -> FAIL at step 05; +3000ms on /api/data/availability -> FAIL at step 10; +6800ms on /api/runs -> FAIL at step 13. The SAME proxy with zero delay PASSES, so the proxy itself is not what fails the run. 
PROVEN NOT TO BE HAIR-TRIGGER: +3000ms on bars and +3000ms on /api/runs both still PASS (the gate trips between +3.0s and +6.2s of added latency, as designed), and the unmodified golden PASSED 3/3 consecutive `demo_runner --mode verify` runs on an idle host AND 3/3 more with 2 of this 4-core host's CPUs deliberately pinned at 100% (load average 2.7), where the assertion steps still used only 0.01-0.06s of their 2000ms windows. That directly retires the first pass's flakiness worry, which had been mis-attributed to endpoint concurrency on /stocks/AAPL: the real cause of a tight-window failure is the absorption mechanism above, not host noise. 
HONEST SCOPE OF WHAT THIS GOLDEN PROVES: a 4.5s page-level end-to-end bound (2.0s for availability past its own stagger), NOT the literal per-call <=0.1s / <=1.5s budgets -- a Playwright replay measures when a rendered value appears, never the HTTP call in isolation. The precise per-call claims stay where they are instrument-appropriate: isolated curl reads (reports/perf-budgets.md Addendum 21, TC-5/TC-8) and in-browser resource timings (Addendum 22).

ops-hardening iter-57: step 9's fixed 2500ms `wait_for` is NOT a magic number -- it is `apps/frontend/app/data/page.tsx`'s own named `AVAILABILITY_FETCH_STAGGER_MS` constant (the deliberate stagger past the coverage/index-vendor panels' own on-mount fetches, iter-6/J-06), read directly from source. Without first consuming this real, product-code-owned delay, step 10's window would start its clock before the availability fetch has even begun, and would FAIL on every replay regardless of backend speed -- a false regression, not a real one. If a future iteration changes that constant, this step must be updated to match (recorded here so the two never silently drift).
